questions.q: Why does the Silver transformation call dropDuplicates(["order_id", "line_number"]) instead of dropDuplicates() with no arguments?
options: Naming the real business key catches rows that represent the same sale line item even if some other column differs slightly between copies
dropDuplicates() with no arguments is not valid PySpark syntax
Because order_id and line_number are the only two columns Bronze contains
Because Delta tables require at least two columns in every dropDuplicates call
questions.explain: A plain dropDuplicates() only removes rows that are completely identical across every column, which rarely catches real-world duplicate sale line items.

questions.q: Why does Silver use explicit type casts like .cast("decimal(12,2)") instead of relying on inferSchema the way Bronze did?
options: Because Gold's aggregation next lesson depends on sales_amount actually being a number it can sum correctly
Because Delta tables cannot store inferred types
Because explicit casts run faster than any other PySpark operation
Because inferSchema is only available for JSON files, not CSV
questions.explain: Bronze didn't need the guess to be exact, but Silver's numbers feed directly into the final daily total, so the type must be declared on purpose.

questions.q: Which three columns does this lesson treat as required, and drop rows that are missing any of them?
options: store_id, sale_date, and sales_amount
order_id, line_number, and channel
customer_name, email, and phone_number
product_category, region, and discount_code
questions.explain: Those three are the columns Gold's aggregation cannot function without — no date, amount, or store ID means the row contributes nothing measurable.

questions.q: Why does the Silver write use mode("overwrite") instead of mode("append")?
options: Silver recomputes from the entirety of Bronze every run, so it only needs to be correct right now, not keep its own independent history
overwrite mode is required by Delta Lake for all Silver-layer tables
append mode would double the row count of the Gold table
Because Bronze no longer exists after Silver is written
questions.explain: Unlike Bronze, which preserves history, Silver is a derived, recomputed view of the current state of Bronze — full overwrite is correct for this Beginner pipeline.

questions.q: What real limitation does this lesson name out loud about using overwrite instead of an incremental MERGE?
options: Every run recomputes everything from scratch rather than processing only new or changed data, which a later project's incremental design will fix
Overwrite mode permanently deletes the Bronze table
Overwrite mode cannot be used with Delta Lake at all
Overwrite mode is incompatible with Spark SQL
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly flags that an incremental MERGE instead of full overwrite is the next project's real improvement, not something this Beginner pipeline hides or ignores.
